evidence: the-container-is-killed (manifests/docker_container.pp:82-93): docker::run declares the container under the module's systemd unit (run.pp systemd_restart default 'on-failure', remove_container_on_stop => false keeps the container to start again); the kill is a crash stimulus, not something the class runs, and its effect only shows the start time was noted - the kill's real result is judged by the-service-starts-it-again (a new StartedAt, running), so the pair is sound; mutates declares the /run/p8test-docker note and the kill, nothing else

the-container-runs-the-image-under-systemd (82-84, with 42-46): under the params fixture (image nginx, tag alpine) image_id = 'nginx:alpine' and docker::run title docker_container; the probe reads the pulled image's tag, the unit docker-docker_container (module service_prefix 'docker-' + title, run.pp:217/511) is active, and the running container uses nginx:alpine - exactly what the lines declare

the-app-answers-on-loopback-only (52-54): with app_port 80 and host_port 18080 myapp_port = ['127.0.0.1:18080:80']; the probe checks docker port mapping, that the only listener on 18080 is 127.0.0.1, and nginx's heading answers there; the mismatch varies only the curl address to the host-only address (enp0s8), which must fail when the bind is loopback-only and would pass if the port were published on all addresses - a real verdict change, it failed after apply as required

Tested on the applied node: image pulled at the tag, container running from it as systemd unit docker-<title>, port published on 127.0.0.1:18080 only with nginx answering, and a killed container started again by its service (module on-failure restart).
